overview: Mawgan Porth is a lovely, sandy beach where the River Menalhyl meets the sea, about four miles north of Newquay, backed by dunes with cliffs at either end. It’s a great all-rounder: lifeguards in summer, surf, a car park, café and toilets right by the beach, and no Council dog restriction.
The little settlement behind it has a pub, a shop and a handful of places to stay, and the coast path heads north along the clifftops to the famous stacks at Bedruthan.

expect.title: Sand and surf
expect.text: A sandy, dune-backed beach that’s popular for surfing.

expect.title: The river
expect.text: The River Menalhyl runs out across the beach, with shallow water for paddling.

expect.title: Coast path
expect.text: Walk north along the clifftops to Carnewas for the view of the Bedruthan stacks.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: North of Watergate Bay, about four miles north of Newquay.

week.text: A family-friendly beach day that dog owners will appreciate in high summer. Combine it with the clifftop walk to Bedruthan for the view.

pairWith.why: the clifftop viewpoint over the Bedruthan stacks
a small cove just round the headland
a peaceful garden in St Mawgan

tips: Stay for sunset: the beach faces west.
